messages:
tess: FYI received an ops alert: recon delta spike after yesterday's ledger compaction job. small magnitude but shows up as duplicate credit assignments for ~12 tenants.
omar: can you paste a compact example of the bad event?
tess: pasted snippet in logs: 
```
{ envelope_v1: { eventId: 'e-942', tenant: null, region: 'us-east-1' }, payload: {...} }
// later transformed into ledger claim: claimId=null, lease=granted
```
kevin: looking at this, it seems we still have some paths emitting the old envelope without `originTenant` and `claimKey`. recon falls back to event-hash which collides with a rehydration case.
joy: is the root cause emission error, or the finalizer/handback semantics?
tess: mixed. two contributing flows: (A) runtime optimistic-claim on hot-path that writes a soft-claim to ledger; (B) async finalizer that may reassign a token if lease tombstone abused earlier. If (A) and (B) interleave across regions we get duplicates.
omar: options: 1) strengthen handback (single-writer per-token) 2) keep optimistic-claim + stronger dedupe in recon 3) add a short-lived inflight lease that prevents finalizer racing.
kevin: 1 is simplest for correctness but hurts latency and complicates cross-region handoffs. 2 keeps latency but moves complexity to audits and backfill. 3 is compromise: low-latency but GC fiddly.
joy: product/finance ask: what is tolerable exposure? can we have bounded eventual reconciliations with guaranteed refund window?
omar: finance wants hard guarantees for enterprise. for self-serve we can accept small transient diffs if we publish corrections in an audit export within 24h.
tess: proposal: implement deterministic `claimKey` on every claim RPC: `claimKey = sha256(tenantId + '|' + eventId + '|' + originEpoch)`; use it in ledger entries and in proofframe. Recon will prefer claimKey when deduping.
kevin: +1. also add `handbackMode` per-tenant: [strict, relaxed]. strict = single-writer (strong CAS), relaxed = optimistic + recon. Default relaxed for self-serve, strict for enterprise.
joy: need telemetry: overcharge_count, overcharge_amount_usd, mean_reconcile_lag, percent_reconciled_within_24h. Ops need alerts on >5 tenants affected in 1h.
omar: infra note: to support canary we need a feature-flag gate + rollout plan. canary 5-10% tenants on strict.
ci-bot: triggered job: integration/ledger/claimKey-roundtrip (region-fuzz) 
ci-bot: job passed (4 variants), 1 flaky variant failing intermittently. full logs: https://ci.internal/runs/4661239999
kevin: the flaky variant is cross-region clock skew. parser should accept tolerances and reconciler should accept small epoch deltas (<10s) without remapping tenant shards.
tess: additional safety: short inflight marker on claim write for 2s to block finalizer reaper. TTL-based so GC is automatic. meant purely as defense-in-depth for relaxed mode.
omar: agree. implement inflight marker as ephemeral key in the same KV (co-located) so it's cheap. also add a metric `lease_reaper_blocked_by_inflight`.
joy: ops wants an audit export format for corrections. prefer a CSV with: tenant, eventId, originalCharge, correctedCharge, reconcileTs, reason. Also an API endpoint for customers to pull corrections.
deploy-bot: (typo) oops
deploy-bot: FYI: rolling patch to ledger service queued for canary cluster at 02:00 UTC.
kevin: tests required before merge: property tests for claimKey uniqueness, integration e2e with finalizer + reaper, backfill dry-run that rewrites claimKey for last 30d.
audits-team: pls review backfill mapping early. any rewrite of proofframe must be signed-off.
tess: action items:
- tess: open RFC PR describing claimKey, handbackMode, inflight marker, API changes + perf baseline (today)
- kevin: add claimKey implementation + unit tests (48h)
- omar: infra for feature-flag canary + alerting hooks (48h)
- joy: define customer-visible correction API and notification copy (end of week)
- audits-team: review backfill mapping when RFC posted
kevin: note: we should schedule a 30m sync with finance before canary flip.
tess: will schedule. ping here when RFC is up. :white_check_mark:
